data.title: mTORC1 couples immune signals and metabolic programming to establish T(reg)-cell function
data.authors: Zeng H; Chi H et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTORC1 couples immune signals and metabolism to establish regulatory T-cell function.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway integrates diverse environmental inputs, including immune signals and metabolic cues, to direct T-cell fate decisions. The activation of mTOR, which is the catalytic subunit of the mTORC1 and mTORC2 complexes, delivers an obligatory signal for the proper activation and differentiation of effector CD4(+) T cells, whereas in the regulatory T-cell (T(reg)) compartment, the Akt-mTOR axis is widely acknowledged as a crucial negative regulator of T(reg)-cell de novo differentiation and population expansion.

extracted_findings.effect: mTORC1 couples immune signals and metabolic programming to establish regulatory T-cell function
extracted_findings.limitations: Normal health status of Cd4 cre Raptor fl/fl mice was likely due to impaired activation of conventional T cells, to be described elsewhere.
